text:
🚨🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum to Trump: no one judges Mexico from the outside</u>

After Trump's proclamation branding Mexico a drug-transit country and demanding it arrest officials tied to organized crime, Sheinbaum didn't blink: "We don't need to be judged from outside — we know Mexico's problems, we act on them every day, and we report it." She added she'd like to see a report on what the US itself does. Her government has moved against organized crime and against public servants colluding with it, with results published daily — no foreign proclamation required.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico seizes 59 million liters of stolen fuel — biggest bust of the sexenio</u>

In San José Iturbide, Guanajuato, the FGR and federal security forces cracked the largest fuel-theft seizure of Sheinbaum's term: 59 million liters of huachicol — 33.5M of regular gasoline, 7.3M premium, 18.3M diesel — stashed at a diesel-and-gasoline distributor near federal highway 57, along with 10 storage tanks. It dwarfs the previous record of 15.48 million liters seized in Coahuila in July 2025.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>FED HIKES FOR THE FIRST TIME SINCE 2023; PESO SLIPS TO 17.25</u>

US inflation is reaccelerating, so the Federal Reserve pushed rates to 3.75–4.00% — its first hike since 2023 — and flagged another, brushing off Trump's public demands to cut. El Financiero reports the peso eased to 17.25 per dollar after weeks below 17, with Banxico now expected to pause its own rate-cutting cycle.

🇲🇽✊ <u>THE WOMEN WHO FINANCED MEXICO'S INDEPENDENCE — AND GOT ERASED</u>

As Mexico marks 216 years since the 1810 uprising, historian Pedro Salmerón (UNAM) revisits the insurgentas the textbooks skip: Leona Vicario, who bankrolled the rebellion and smuggled arms and printing type to the rebels; Gertrudis Bocanegra, shot by a firing squad in Pátzcuaro in 1817 for refusing to betray them. Independence wasn't only won by generals on horseback.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN-ERA TAMAULIPAS COMPTROLLER CONVICTED OF CORRUPTION</u>

Tamaulipas's accountability court found Elda Viñas — comptroller under PAN ex-governor García Cabeza de Vaca — guilty of abusing her office: she authorized honoraria for a subordinate who was simultaneously drawing an administrative director's salary. The official once tasked with policing graft now faces prison, fines and disqualification at sentencing on Sep 22.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>MEXICO FUNDS 19 NEW HIGHWAYS: 213.9 BILLION PESOS, 17 STATES</u>

Banobras is bankrolling 19 highway projects across 17 states — 213.868 billion pesos (~$12.4B) and roughly 177,000 direct jobs — as construction runs 6.7% higher year-on-year. Bank chief Jorge Mendoza stresses the mixed-investment model "does not represent concessions where the State completely cedes its rights."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>JAPAN RETURNS A STOLEN MEXICAN MASK — A FIRST</u>

A Japanese collector who bought a Mexican ceremonial mask in France handed it back to Mexico's embassy in Tokyo — the first voluntary return of Mexican heritage ever achieved in Japan. Ambassador Melba Pría received the piece; the collector, now elderly, said it "needs to return home, to be safe."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>TRUMP DEMANDS MEXICO ARREST ITS OWN 'NARCO-OFFICIALS'</u>

In his annual drug report to Congress, Trump conceded Mexico's cooperation helped eliminate cartel bosses "including El Mencho" — then demanded Sheinbaum "expose, arrest and prosecute" the officials Washington deems dirty. Sheinbaum: "Any pretext for interference or intervention must be rejected; it violates our sovereignty and our independence."

🇲🇽🌎 "Any pretext for interference or intervention must be rejected — it violates our sovereignty and our independence." Sheinbaum walked through Mexico's history of foreign interventions — Spain, France, the U.S. that took more than half the territory, 1914 — and how the people fought each one. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on sovereignty "We can always cooperate, they can help us... but the decisions are made by the people, the decisions are made by the government."
